text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:

- The budget crisis in Bonn damages relationships between ruling coalition parties as junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) criticise Finance Minister Theo Waigels's tax plans aimed at solving the crisis.
- Struggling German first division side Hamburg sack their trainer Felix Magath after 0-4 defeat at Cologne on Saturday.
- Head of the German Federation of Trade Unions (DGB) Dieter Schulte calls on individual unions to give up their opposition to reform of industry wide wage agreements.
- Budget problems divide ruling coalition with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's party tending to favour a hike in petrol taxes while junior partners the FDP resist any tax hikes.
- Deputy leader of Germany's largest trade union IG Metall says government plans to sell more Deutsche Telekom shares justifiable.
- DGB's Schulte wants to modernise system of induestry wide wage agreements.
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) set for innovation congress beginning on Tuesday in Duesseldorf intended to give the party a new, more modern image.
- Heads of Kirch media group, Bertelsmann and Deutsche Telekom set to agree on television of the future after years of wrangling, with an accord on the use of digital television with 150 channels.
- DGB head Schulte calls for flexible industry wage contracts.
- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber calls on Prague to set date for German-Czech talks and says representative of Germans expelled from Czech lands after World War Two should take part in them .
- German Trade Union Federation (DGB) distances itself from the SPD by calling for lower pensions and taxation of higher old age income.
- President of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) Alexandre Lamfalussy warns against a delay to the start of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
- Budget holes divide ruling colaltion with the FDP vehemently against tax increases.
